caption:
Your balance, your username, your score: to a program they're all just labeled boxes called variables. And every box has a size limit, which is where crypto bugs begin 🧙

Day 1 of learning crypto security from zero.

Free cheat sheet: 10 crypto hacks explained. Link in bio.

#learntocode #cs50 #cprogramming #solidity #smartcontracts #codingjourney

scenes.h: Every app is just *boxes* with names.
scenes.say: Your balance, your username, your score. To a program, they're all *boxes* with names.
In C, a *variable* has a type, a name, and a value. Coins equals three. Add one, and you get *four*.

scenes.h: Each box holds one kind of thing.
scenes.say: The type says what fits. *int* for whole numbers, *char* for one character, *string* for text.
The catch: every box has a size *limit*. A thirty two bit int stops near two point one billion. Push past it, and you get *overflow*.

scenes.sub: Token balances in Solidity are *uint256*: whole numbers, no minus sign, 256 bits.
scenes.say: In Solidity, a token balance is usually a *uint*, two hundred fifty six bits. And overflow bugs have cost real projects real money.
Next up, if and conditions. Follow the journey.
